items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The diff is small and readable and matches the existing style. But the message raise ValueError("Cannot filter a query once a slice has been taken.") in Prefetch.__init__ confuses users: no filter is being applied at that point, and it reuses the TypeError message from QuerySet.filter.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It copies the filter() error string into Prefetch instead of reusing it. It also hard-codes a restriction the issue asked to remove, so a later fix has to undo it. The related_descriptors helper was not touched. The agent's test locks in the wrong behavior: test_sliced_queryset expects ValueError.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Rejecting input up front, at construction time, is defensive and swallows no errors. But it raises a different exception type than filter() does (ValueError vs TypeError) for the same message, and it blocks a valid use case instead of handling it.

items.name: Per-parent slice semantics for open/bounded slices
items.name_zh: 开放/有界切片按父对象分区
items.evidence: No per-parent slicing at all. `if queryset.query.is_sliced: raise ValueError(...)` forbids sliced Prefetch querysets instead of supporting them. There is no Window/RowNumber and no handling of low_mark or high_mark. Hidden tests: F2P 0/4 (PrefetchLimitTests failed).
